title: PhySense: Sensor Placement Optimization for Accurate Physics Sensing

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof claims that by the arithmetic–geometric mean inequality, (Σ√λ_i)^2 ≤ 2Σλ_i. This is false for d>2: for λ=(1,1,1), the left side is 9 and the right side is 6. Since the physical fields here are high-dimensional (6,144 to 95,428 mesh points), the derived bounds 2/π² L_flow² ≤ L_A ≤ 4/π² L_flow² are invalid, so Theorem 3.5 is not established.

Assumption 3.2 states X1 | (p,X1(p)) ≈ N(μ_p, Σ_p), but Appendix A.2 Part 1 says 'Because X1 | (p,X1(p)) ~ N(0, Σ_p)' and sets Z = (X0, X1) with Σ_Z = diag(I, Σ_p). The nonzero conditional mean μ_p is silently dropped, so the covariance calculations and Theorem 3.5 hold only for a centered conditional field, not for the general assumption stated.

The remark claims L_D and L_E are polynomially bounded above and below by L_A using standard spectral inequalities. This is not true in general: L_A=Σλ_i, L_D=Πλ_i, L_E=maxλ_i. For eigenvalues (1,0,…,0), L_A=1 but L_D=0; for (1,1,…,1), L_A=d but L_E=1. Thus no dimension-independent two-sided polynomial bounds exist.

The abstract and Remark 3.6 claim 'theoretical guarantees' and 'a theoretical guarantee for achieving near A-optimal sensor placement,' but Theorem 3.5 explicitly says the relation 'should be treated as a heuristic rather than strict guarantee,' and the appendix proof of the theorem is mathematically invalid. The guarantee language overstates the evidence.

The text states that 'subsequent analyses (Appendix D) reveal that performance degrades notably at very low sensor numbers (below 10), and variance across runs increases.' However, Appendix D.3 is titled '10–200' but contains only #200, #100, #50, #30, and #15; no results below 10 sensors are reported anywhere.

The section claims: 'Ablations also include systematic sensitivity analyses to key training hyperparameters such as learning rate, optimizer type, and projected gradient descent iteration counts.' The appendix reports only learning-rate sensitivity (Table 13); no optimizer-type ablation or PGD-iteration-count ablation is provided.

Section 4 says 'epoch counts range between 3 and 10... Exact iteration counts are detailed in Appendix C.3,' but Appendix C.3 only says 'All models are trained for 5 epochs' and gives no per-benchmark exact iteration counts. This contradicts the main text and omits the promised reproducibility details.

The main text claims 'All methods of each benchmark maintain identical training configurations including epochs, batch sizes, ADAM optimizer, and maximum learning rate,' but Appendix C.3 states that Senseiver 'did not strictly enforce the same training epoch limit' and was trained until its default early stopping criterion triggered. Thus the claimed controlled comparison is false.

The baseline reported as VoronoiCNN [14] in Table 2 is not the original method: the paper states 'We replace it with a more powerful U-Net architecture.' This modified architecture is not identified as 'VoronoiCNN-U' or otherwise distinguished, which misrepresents the baseline in the main comparison.
